sections.heading: C — Rural, Night, Sharing, Weather
sections.markdown:
## C — Rural, Night, Sharing, Weather

FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Meet gravel oncoming on narrow unmarked lanes by slowing, hugging right as safe, and braving dust clouds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
Treat rural bridges as one-car squeezes narrower than the road, stopping for oncoming users [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
Pre-slow and right-hug before hill crests and curves, which run steeper and sharper off-highway [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
Cross rural tracks only after slowing, double-looking, and readying to stop, since lights, bells, gates, and markings usually miss [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
Farm rigs, ATVs, bikes, horse carts, and work crews creep rural roads, so spot them early, slow down, and pass farm giants with extreme care past their wide unmarked turns, road-wide bodies, and faint signals [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
Dark driving slows pace, stretches gaps, fights glare by right-looking and mirror tilts, lights up before sunset, saves high beams for lonely roads, and answers blinding with slower speed and right-edge stripes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A02
Watch animals hardest at dawn and dusk; given no stop room, hold course since swerves worsen crashes, and after strikes run crash protocol [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A02
Deer top Iowa wildlife crashes, peaking in October, November, and May yet striking year-round in groups that demand extra scanning [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A02
Car riders absorb 78 percent of truck-crash deaths, so grant big rigs wide respect and shun their front, back, and side no-zones, remembering mirror invisibility cuts both ways [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A02
Trucks out-brake you in distance, so re-enter only past a mirror-full truck nose and never cut their bows [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A02
Right-turning trucks first swing left, blind to tail and flank sitters, so never thread truck and curb and mind their signals [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A03
Honor motorcycle space, treat intersections as prime collision ground by confirming sight and speed, and distrust sticky signals until intent shows [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A03
Trail bikes by three to four seconds, farther when wet for two-wheel wobble, and pass only with full spare lanes unshared [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A03
Scan intersections and drives for walkers, riders, skaters, wheelchairs, and micro-devices, then yield them the right-of-way [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A03
Never overtake cars stopped or slowing for pedestrians you cannot yet see [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A03
Bikes belong on roads, often barred from sidewalks, so pass only via full lane changes and return right only past mirror-visible riders [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F17 | anchor: A03
Hunt night reflectors and lights plus rear blind spots, hardest before right turns [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F18 | anchor: A04
Never cage kids, elders, dependents, or pets in parked cars, whose cabins top 160 degrees within 10 minutes and hit 100 on mild 78-degree days; heatstroke kills, so call 911 and know Iowa lets rescuers smash windows [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec16-F19 | anchor: A04
Pre-study weather trips via Iowa traveler info online and in-app around the clock, scouting plow and traffic cameras firsthand [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec16-F20 | anchor: A04
Forced into storms, slow down, stretch gaps, kill cruise, maintain the car, and pack a winter emergency kit [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec16-F21 | anchor: A05
Wet roads want prompt wipers, low beams, slower pace, five-to-six-second gaps, gentle curves and crossings, defrosted glass, dead cruise, and only clear-road one-second glances [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F22 | anchor: A05
Water past tread depth planes tires into skids, so slow at deep puddles, shiny pavement, or vanished leader tracks [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F23 | anchor: A05
Vehicles account for nearly half of flash-flood deaths. As little as six inches of moving water may carry a vehicle away, including a sport utility vehicle or pickup. Do not cross a flooded roadway or bridge; turn back and choose another route. Leave a vehicle that stalls in floodwater and head to higher ground. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F24 | anchor: A05
Swept under, stay calm, let the cabin flood, push doors open, hold breath, and swim up [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F25 | anchor: A05
Fog wants low or fog beams never high ones, sight-matched speed, and parking off-road when needed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F26 | anchor: A05
Tornado watches mean possible twisters and warnings mean imminent ones via broadcasts, radios, and sirens; drivers best shelter in sturdy buildings [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F27 | anchor: A05
Shelterless, pull over, duck belted below glass shielding heads, or ditch-crouch after safe exits, always shunning bridges and overpasses [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec16-F28 | anchor: A06
Strip every flake off glass and lamps, and fear invisible black ice, which bridges and overpasses grow first from double-sided frost [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec16-F29 | anchor: A06
Launch straight and gentle, slow for lost grip, kill cruise, brake early only rolling straight, and hang far back against tenfold stops and skids [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec16-F30 | anchor: A06
Plows plod near 25 to 35 mph inviting rear-enders, so approach gently, never pass shoulder-side, grant blind spotted snowy room, and pass wide of jutting blades [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec16-F31 | anchor: A06
Snowbound, shoulder-park, stay belted inside as findable shelter, and phone 911 with exits, mileposts, or landmarks [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0061]

Misconceptions: high beams cut fog, yet they blind you with glare; floodwater looks passable, yet inches can float a truck; swerving saves animals, yet it worsens crashes.

Mnemonic: night low and long, trucks wide berth, bikes full lane, ice tenfold, floods turn round.

Glossary: no-zone (a truck blind spot); black ice (a near-invisible frozen film); hydroplaning (tires planing on water past tread depth); tornado warning (an imminent tornado demanding shelter).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every rural, night, sharing, and weather rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
